phases.title: Foundations — securities & market structure
phases.summary: Understand what a security is, how U.S. markets are organized, and who regulates each layer before you touch capital or code.
topics: Stocks, bonds, ETFs, options, futures — and which agency governs each
Primary vs secondary market; exchanges (NYSE, Nasdaq) vs ATS/dark pools
Market participants: retail investor, accredited investor, institution, broker-dealer, RIA
Key laws: Securities Act 1933, Exchange Act 1934, Investment Advisers Act 1940

resources.label: SEC — U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission

phases.title: Personal trading — accounts, rules & taxes
phases.summary: Open a brokerage account, learn order types, pattern-day-trader limits, and tax reporting before automating anything.
topics: Brokerage account types: cash, margin, IRA, 401(k) — each has different rules
FINRA margin & Pattern Day Trader (PDT) rule — 4+ day trades in 5 days on margin
Order types: market, limit, stop, stop-limit; time-in-force (DAY, GTC)
Wash-sale rule (IRS), cost basis, Form 1099-B, capital gains short vs long term
SIPC protection — what it covers (securities in brokerage failure, not investment loss)

phases.title: Research & market data — EDGAR, 13F, insider filings
phases.summary: Use public filings to understand Forbes-list company stakes, insider activity, and institutional positioning — the data layer your bot will consume.
topics: SEC EDGAR — 10-K, 10-Q, 8-K, proxy (DEF 14A), S-1 IPO filings
Form 4 — insider buys/sells within 2 business days (Section 16)
Schedule 13D/13G — 5%+ beneficial ownership
Form 13F — institutional managers with $100M+ AUM (quarterly holdings)
Reg FD — no selective disclosure; use only public information for algo signals

phases.title: Algorithmic trading — architecture & market rules
phases.summary: Design bots with audit trails, kill switches, and awareness of market-structure rules before going live.
topics: Paper trading & backtesting — never skip; document assumptions and slippage
Market manipulation prohibitions: spoofing, layering, wash trades (SEC Rule 10b-5, CFTC)
Reg NMS — order protection, best execution obligations (broker responsibility)
Reg SCI — systems compliance for exchanges and large market participants
Algo audit trail: order logs, timestamps, strategy version, config hash
API rate limits, circuit breakers, and exchange halts (LULD)

phases.title: Licensing & registration — when you need exams
phases.summary: Trading your own account needs no license; managing others' money or acting as a broker-dealer requires registration and exams.
topics: No license needed: personal account, your own capital, no advice to others
SIE (Securities Industry Essentials) — gateway exam for industry roles
Series 7 — general securities representative (broker-dealer)
Series 63 — state securities law (often paired with 7 or 65)
Series 65/66 — investment adviser representative (RIA channel)
RIA registration: Form ADV with SEC (>$100M AUM) or state (<$100M)
Broker-dealer registration: FINRA member firm + SEC registration

phases.title: Compliant trading bot — production checklist
phases.summary: Cross every T before live capital: recordkeeping, supervision, AML, cybersecurity, and Forbes-lister-specific filing awareness.
topics: Recordkeeping: SEC Rule 17a-4 (3-6 year retention for broker-dealers); keep bot logs regardless
Supervision: FINRA Rule 3110 if operating through a BD; written supervisory procedures
AML/BSA: FinCEN if handling client funds; SAR filing for suspicious activity
OFAC sanctions screening on counterparties and jurisdictions
Cybersecurity: SEC cybersecurity disclosure rules; CISA guidance for financial infrastructure
Marketing compliance: no guaranteed returns; performance claims need disclaimers (SEC Marketing Rule)
Forbes lister crosswalk: map each ticker to insider (Form 4), 13F, and material-event (8-K) obligations

forbesRules.title: Form 4 — insider transactions
forbesRules.trigger: Officer, director, or 10%+ owner buys/sells company stock
forbesRules.botImpact: Do not trade on non-public insider knowledge; monitor public Form 4s as signals only

forbesRules.title: Form 13F — institutional holdings
forbesRules.trigger: Investment manager with >$100M in qualifying assets
forbesRules.botImpact: Track which institutions hold Forbes tickers; your bot may need 13F if AUM threshold met

forbesRules.title: Schedule 13D / 13G — 5%+ ownership
forbesRules.trigger: Beneficial ownership crosses 5% of any class of equity
forbesRules.botImpact: Aggregated bot + personal holdings may trigger if controlling stake

forbesRules.title: Rule 10b-5 — anti-fraud / insider trading
forbesRules.botImpact: Bot data feeds must be public-only; no MNPI in signal pipeline

forbesRules.title: FINRA Rule 3110 — supervision
forbesRules.trigger: Broker-dealer member firm deploying algo strategies
forbesRules.botImpact: BD must supervise algo; retail API users inherit BD compliance

forbesRules.title: SEC Rule 17a-4 — record retention
forbesRules.botImpact: Keep immutable bot logs, order history, config versions

forbesRules.title: Pattern Day Trader rule
forbesRules.trigger: 4+ day trades in 5 business days in margin account under $25K
forbesRules.botImpact: High-frequency retail bots may trigger PDT freeze

forbesRules.title: Form ADV — investment adviser registration
forbesRules.botImpact: Bot giving signals to paying subscribers may require RIA registration

botChecklist.label: Kill switch & max-loss circuit breaker implemented
Immutable audit log (orders, signals, config hash)
Data pipeline uses only public sources (no MNPI)
Broker verified via FINRA BrokerCheck + SIPC member
PDT / margin requirements understood for strategy frequency
Tax reporting workflow (1099-B, wash sales) configured
OFAC / sanctions screening if international counterparties
RIA registration assessed if advising others for fee
No guaranteed-return claims; performance disclaimers ready
Forbes ticker crosswalk completed for each held symbol
